CAUSE: Kalshi sharded its matching engine. Its READ endpoints aggregate across shards; its WRITE endpoints do not. Every cancel went out unrouted, so a cancel for an order resting on a non-default shard was answered 404 not_found permanently. One order sat 3.5 days past its timeout, alive at queue rank 1 in the same second a cancel was refused.

FIXED IN THREE PRs: #368 recorded the diagnosis; #370 put the error class and body into the log message so the cause became readable at all (it had been written to a structured field the log service drops); #377 routed the timeout cancel using the market's own exchange_index, which Kalshi documents as authoritative; #380 extended that to the drain and queue-aware cancels and added a failure counter.

VALIDATED IN PRODUCTION, not in a fixture: the specific order that opened this ticket cancelled on the first reconcile cycle after #377 deployed, and the post-#380 soak is clean on every counter.
